name: Leaf Green
lede: Leaf green is the yellowish green of young leaves, and also, in the pigment trade, an old name for a durable pale green made from chromium.

sections.title: The color of young leaves
sections.body:
The Dictionary of Colour defines leaf green as the color of leaves, sometimes the yellowy green of young leaves, and notes that it is one of the colors in the Ostwald circle [1]. The swatch here is a vivid yellow-green. Close neighbors are [[grass-green]], [[lime-green]] and [[moss-green]] [5]. Ridgway's 1912 nomenclature for naturalists has it, and so do the German RAL list (1927) and the ISCC-NBS system (1955) [5].

The name has a mineral echo. Malachite takes its name from the Greek word for mallow, referring to its leaf-green color [2]. See [[malachite]].

sections.title: A chromium pigment
sections.body: As a pigment name, leaf green was described in 1874 by Riffault and colleagues as a durable pale green, made by heating chromic oxide with aluminium hydroxide [3]. Mayer's 1991 handbook simply treats it as a synonym of chrome green [3]. Another pigment reference lists it with a group of green and yellow pigments built on chromium, Prussian blue and related compounds [4]. Compare [[viridian]].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive this exact green is nearly absent: 1 painting out of 23,781, rarer than 86 percent of named colors, as photographed [5]. These are photographs of varnished paintings, so a bright green may read differently from how it was painted [5].
